title: Finite coproducts of coherent topoi are componentwise coherent
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set and let $(\mathcal E_i)_{i\in I}$ be Grothendieck topoi, with small-site presentations $\mathcal E_i\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_i)$ in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Sites and sheaves of sets have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Define the disjoint-union site $\mathcal C$ to have objects $(i,U)$ with $U\in\mathcal C_i$, morphisms $(i,U)\to(i,V)$ the morphisms $U\to V$ of $\mathcal C_i$, no morphisms between different components, and coverings exactly the coverings within a component. Put $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$. Restriction to the components gives an equivalence $\mathcal E\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal E_i$. Under it, limits, colimits and epimorphisms are componentwise. The geometric morphism $j_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal E$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism] has inverse image $(A_k)_k\mapsto A_i$ and right adjoint placing $A_i$ in component $i$ and the terminal object in every other component. These morphisms exhibit $\mathcal E$ as the coproduct $\coprod_i\mathcal E_i$ of topoi: a family of geometric morphisms $u_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal F$ induces $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, unique up to the compatible natural isomorphism, with
$$u^{-1}A=(u_i^{-1}A)_i,\qquad u_*(B_i)_i=\prod_i u_{i,*}B_i,\qquad uj_i\simeq u_i.$$
This construction is independent of the presentations up to equivalence. If every $\mathcal E_i$ is coherent in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos], then $\mathcal E$ is coherent, and an object $(A_i)_i$ is coherent if and only if every $A_i$ is coherent. For $I=\varnothing$ the construction is the degenerate topos with one object and one arrow.

source.place: Agent formulation of the finite coproduct construction from Definition 00VH (definition-site), the set-sheaf equalizer condition 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets), limits 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf) and colimits 00WI (lemma-colimit-sheaves); the coherence assertion uses the explicit quasi-compact/quasi-separated definitions in def-trf-coherent-topos. These sources supply the construction tools, rather than a named coproduct-coherence theorem.
